result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer A recommends checking a field once the person leaves it, then re-checking it live after an error appears, and it gives each field a concrete behavior, which covers the rubric well. Answer B has strong extras (accessibility, autocomplete, keeping the submit button active) and handles the username and password well. However, it explicitly rejects checking on leaving the field and leaves email to be checked only on submit. That goes against rubric item 2 and partly recreates the pile of errors at the end. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B explains both failure modes: false errors while someone is still typing, and a pile of problems discovered at submit. It recommends checking on blur, re-checking live once an error shows, a debounced username check that cancels stale requests, and showing the password rule up front. A does well on live re-checking and the per-field exceptions, but it explicitly rejects checking when someone leaves a field. It also leans on submit-only checking and barely mentions the problem of finding everything wrong at the end.
